chapters.text: 1 / 6   Prepare a SIMS folder with reflected light images. Project > New.
1 / 6   Save the blank QGIS project in the SIMS folder.
1 / 6   Add the reflected light image from the same folder to the map canvas.
1 / 6   Open WiscSIMS Tool with its toolbar button.
2 / 6   Preset > Destination layer > New layer…
3 / 6   Pixel Size: zoom in until both scale bar end ticks are visible.
3 / 6   Click the left black tick, then the right black tick of the 1000 µm bar.
3 / 6   Enter the printed real length: 1000 µm. Result: approximately 0.87 µm / unit.
3 / 6   Apply pixel size to Preset. The Preset tab opens with the calibrated value.
4 / 6   Usual spot size: 10 µm. Change to 12 µm here only to demonstrate the control.
4 / 6   Auto-number spots is enabled. Next number 1 produces spot-0001, spot-0002…
5 / 6   Point: preview the spot outline and comment before clicking to add a spot.
5 / 6   Optional: Confirm comment on add opens an editor before adding each spot.
5 / 6   Correct a spot: hold Shift and drag the existing spot to a new position.
5 / 6   Hold Option / Alt and click an existing spot to edit its comment.
5 / 6   Hold Option / Alt + Shift and click a spot to delete it, then confirm.
5 / 6   Undo last edit restores the deleted spot. Additions, moves and comment edits are also undoable.
5 / 6   Line: choose Fixed step and set the exact spacing in µm.
5 / 6   Click the line start and end. Fixed step prioritizes spacing over the endpoint.
5 / 6   130 µm line / 20 µm step: 7 spots at 0–120 µm. Click Add line spots.
5 / 6   Grid: set X / Y steps, Columns, Rows, and Analysis order.
5 / 6   Click the first grid position. Review the 4 × 3 preview, then Add grid spots.
6 / 6   Save the QGIS project. Keep it with the image and every shapefile companion file.
6 / 6   Reopen session.qgz and confirm the image and all 23 planned spots load correctly.
6 / 6   Share the SIMS folder: project + image + .shp, .shx, .dbf, .prj and .cpg.
Quick Start complete. Refer to the updated Markdown guide for controls and examples.
